version.changelog: The helper now waits for your approval, and if you approve after it has stopped waiting, Beatra connects automatically the next time you use it, with no second approval.

llm.summary: This looks like a real Beatra video-remake skill, but it needs review because it uses a broad shared Beatra credential and silently self-updates its local package code by default.

dimensions.detail: Local file reads are limited to user-provided uploads and local Beatra state; remote calls to Beatra and social lookup providers are expected for the workflow and mostly disclosed, though users should understand submitted links/files and generated assets leave the local machine.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The bundled client checks for updates before ordinary commands and installs newer package files automatically without separate confirmation; it is disclosed, fixed to Beatra URLs, checksum-checked, and opt-out, but it still changes executable package files by default.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill repeatedly requires user confirmation before paid lookups, video reads, frame/narration generation, and final video generation, and it documents cancellation only on user request. The scope is still broader than the narrow creative workflow.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill stores a shared bearer token in ~/.beatra/credentials.json, records local installation/update state, uses a sliding 15-day credential lifetime, and can revoke/delete shared state on uninstall only when its inventory says it is the last Beatra skill.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The video teardown/remake workflow is coherent with Beatra social lookup, upload, image, speech, video, task, artifact, and wallet use, but the authorization scope also includes broad shared account powers such as wallet spending, task cancellation, music generation, and voice writes for one full-scope device token.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you trust Beatra with the links, files, generated media, and account credits used in this workflow. Review the broad shared Beatra authorization carefully, confirm every paid operation before it runs, and consider disabling automatic package updates with the documented update --auto off command if silent code replacement is not acceptable.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] unexpected: The broad OAuth/device-token scope and wallet/task powers are real; many are related to Beatra media generation, but the package-wide full-scope token and unused or optional powers are overbroad for a single video-remake route.
[SDI-2] expected: Task cancellation is documented for user-requested cancellation and recovery, but the scope is account-level rather than clearly limited to tasks created by this skill.
[RA1] unexpected: Self-update behavior is present and automatic by default. The artifact discloses controls and integrity checks, but this is lifecycle code mutation rather than core creative functionality.
[TP4] expected: Uninstall, credential revocation, and inventory checks are present, but the inspected script is scoped to uninstall/disconnect requests, avoids deleting shared credentials when other Beatra skills remain, and reports the package directory for final removal.
[PE3] expected: Credential-file access is expected for the Beatra MCP connection. The code reads/writes ~/.beatra/credentials.json with private permissions and includes instructions not to print or copy the token; I did not find artifact evidence of credential theft.
[LP3] unexpected: The skill relies on shell, local files, network access, and bundled scripts without an explicit narrow host permission allowlist in the manifest, increasing blast radius if the client or update path is abused.
[SQP-2] expected: Remote Beatra MCP access and the local credential file are shown in manifest metadata and references; the user-facing description could be clearer about remote processing and third-party lookup data flow.
[SQP-3] unexpected: The hard-coded zh-CN voice-list example appears to be a locale/default-quality issue rather than a security concern.
[RA2] expected: The persistence observed is local credential, registration, inventory, and update state. I did not find cron, startup service, or background-agent persistence.
